tabbit.enum-label-redefined: Label '{Label}' is already defined in enum '{Enum}'.
tabbit.enum-label-value-not-integer: Label '{Label}' in enum '{Enum}' has value `{Value}`, which is not an integer.
tabbit.constant-redefined: Constant '{Name}' is already defined in constant-set '{Set}'.
tabbit.constant-cannot-be-optional: type `{Type}`: a constant cannot be optional. A constant is a single value, so drop the `?`.
tabbit.enum-needs-detail-type: In case of enum type, enum name must be specified in detail-type.
tabbit.foreign-needs-detail-type: In case of foreign type, `RefTable[.RefFieldName]` must be specified in detail-type.
tabbit.field-name-ambiguous-element-numb: Field name `{Field}` has more than one run of digits in `{Group}`, so which one numbers the elements is ambiguous. Use a single number, as in `Slot1{Separator}Id` or `Pos{Separator}X1`.
tabbit.field-name-element-number-not-int: Field name `{Field}` has element number `{Digits}`, which is not an integer.
tabbit.field-name-multiple-index-marks: Field name `{Field}` has more than one leading `*`. Use a single `*` to mark a secondary index field.
tabbit.primary-index-cannot-be-omitted: The primary index field cannot be omitted.
tabbit.primary-index-in-record-group: The primary index field cannot be part of a record group, but `{Field}` is.
tabbit.record-member-marked-secondary-in: Field name `{Field}` marks a record member as a secondary index. An index must be a single value, so `*` cannot be used on a record group.
tabbit.element-optional-mark-on-non-arra: type `{Type}`: the `?` inside the brackets says an element may have no value, and this column is not an array. Write the `?` at the end to say the value itself may be absent.
tabbit.foreign-array-unsupported: `foreign[]` is not supported. Use a serial field (Ref1, Ref2, ...) for a fixed number of references, or a plain `foreign` for a single one.
tabbit.multi-target-names-a-field: `{Written}` names several tables and also a field of one of them (`{Dotted}`). A reference to one of several tables names the tables alone - drop the field name, or point at them from separate columns.
tabbit.type-not-array-element: type `{Type}` cannot be used as an array element.
tabbit.type-named-twice: Column type `{Type}` already names `{Names}`, and the detail-type cell beside it says `{Written}`. Write it in one of the two.
tabbit.entity-starts-outside-sheet: Entity `{Kind}:{Name}` starts outside the sheet: its marker points at column {Column}, row {Row}, and the sheet holds {Columns} column(s) and {Rows} row(s). A marker in the last cell with nothing after it does this.
tabbit.entity-too-small: Entity `{Kind}:{Name}` must have cells of at least {MinWidth}x{MinHeight} size. The size of the currently accessible cell is {Width}x{Height}.
tabbit.wire-tag-not-positive-integer: Field name `{Field}` has an `@` where a wire tag goes, but `{Digits}` is not a positive integer. A tag is written as `Name@3`.
tabbit.wire-tag-below-one: Field `{Field}` declares wire tag {Tag}, but a tag starts at 1.
